title: The Tryouts of Maple Street
premise: Every fall, Maple Street's high school runs the Tryouts, a century-old tradition that secretly decides who the town invests in and who it forgets. Mirabel Amberdale, the team statistician, has charted the pattern for years: the same families rise, the invisible kids vanish from every record. When a group chat of 'cut' students begins texting predictions that come true hours later, Mirabel realizes the Tryouts run on borrowed time—literally—and that her own erased memories are the currency keeping it alive. To save the town without feeding the tradition another generation, she must expose the ledger at the championship game, sacrificing her own spot in everyone's memory to break the cycle.
about_author: C. M. Sandoval is a former small-town sports statistician who spent three seasons keeping score before realizing some games keep score back. They write YA fiction about quiet kids who notice too much, from a desk covered in old box scores.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Opening day of Tryout season; Mirabel catalogs players, grades, and the eerie consistency of who gets chosen. Establishes their invisibility as armor and their statistical obsession as both gift and shield. Emotional beat: wary comfort in routine, undercut by a nagging sense that the numbers don't add up this year.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A chat titled 'Cut List' appears on their phone with six classmates they barely know—including star pitcher Dev Okafor, who was never cut. The first message predicts tomorrow's rain-out exactly. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding caution; the thrill of being seen by someone, even an algorithm.

chapters.title: Rain on Schedule
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The prediction lands perfectly, and the chat sends a second: Coach Bellamy will bench a sophomore who hasn't been injured yet. He is. Dev drags Mirabel into comparing notes. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve—the two outsiders form an uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the gym's sealed records room, Mirabel finds the Ledger: a hundred years of names, trades, and gaps where memories should be—including pages about their own older sister, whom no one remembers. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through data; the personal cost of the tradition becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: Six of Us, Minus One
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The chat's members meet in person; one, Theo, denies ever joining and by morning has forgotten the group entirely. His name appears in the Ledger under 'paid.' Emotional beat: terror and guilt—the predictions aren't gifts, they're receipts.

chapters.title: The Rigged Bracket
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Semifinals approach; Mirabel's stats prove outcomes are fixed years in advance, seeded by family names. The group debates going public but fears becoming 'paid' like Theo. Emotional beat: fracture in the alliance—Dev wants to play along and survive; Mirabel can't unsee the pattern.

chapters.title: Memory Is a Currency
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel confronts Coach Bellamy, who reveals the Tryouts trade the town's prosperity for its cut kids' futures and memories—and that Mirabel has paid before, which is why their childhood feels hollow. Emotional beat: devastating recognition; invisibility wasn't a choice, it was a withdrawal.

chapters.title: Countdown to Championships
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The chat starts predicting things about the five remaining members themselves. Priya's own future entry surfaces: forgotten by graduation. With time running out, they plan to hijack the championship broadcast with the Ledger. Emotional beat: desperate solidarity forged from shared erasure.

chapters.title: The Final Inning
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Climax. During the championship game, Mirabel takes the mic and reads the Ledger aloud as the tradition tries to collect them mid-sentence—memories dissolving page by page. Dev deliberately loses the rigged game to stall the payout while the crowd hears everything. Emotional beat: sacrifice as defiance; Mirabel fights to stay remembered long enough to finish.

chapters.title: New Scorekeepers
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Resolution. The Ledger burns; the town reels, poorer but honest. Mirabel survives, though pieces of them are gone forever—and the sister's name returns to people's mouths. The group founds a new, transparent record-keeping tradition. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal; identity rebuilt not from what was kept, but from what was chosen.
